Investor

in-VES-ter · noun

Hear It

What It Means

a person who puts money into a business or plan, hoping to get more money back

An investor gave the bike shop money to help it open a second store.

Worked Example

Grandma became an investor in Leo's lemonade stand: she paid for the lemons, and he shared what the stand earned.

Grandma put her own money in first, and got money back later when the stand did well. Putting money in and hoping for more back is what an investor does.

How Investor Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

supporter

supporter: a person who helps a plan succeed

partner

partner: a person who joins in a business

Antonyms

borrower

borrower: a person who takes money and must pay it back

customer

customer: a person who spends money on things to keep

How Strong Is It? — Fan → investor → Owner

Fan vs. investor

Fan vs. investor: Fan is lighter: a fan cheers for a team but does not risk any money on it.

Owner vs. investor

Owner vs. investor: Owner is stronger: the whole business belongs to the owner, not just a small share of it.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — invest

root — invest: to put money into something

suffix — or

suffix — or: a person who does it

Put it together

Put it together: Investor is just invest plus -or, 'a person who.' An actor is a person who acts; an investor is a person who invests.

Use the root in a new word: inventor

Use the root in a new word: inventor: The inventor showed off a machine that folds laundry by itself.
